data.name: Rakesh
data.gender_notes: Rakesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Rakesh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Raja' and 'Kshaya', which mean 'Ruler' and 'Destroyer' respectively. It signifies a powerful and victorious leader who has the ability to destroy obstacles and lead his people to prosperity. In Hindu mythology, Rakesh is an alternative name for Lord Karthikeya, the god of war and medicine, who is believed to ride a chariot drawn by horses and elephants.
data.etymology: Rakesh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ruler of the chariot, leader.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rakesh total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: Rakesh was a famous poet and scholar during the medieval period in India. He is known for his works in Sanskrit literature, particularly in the field of Alankara Shastra or the theory of poetics.

Rakesh is also the name of a character in the Indian epic Mahabharata. He was a charioteer and friend of Bhima, one of the Pandava brothers. In the Kurukshetra war, Rakesh was instrumental in Bhima's victory against his opponent Duryodhana.
